content: Flurandrenolide is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as itching, redness, dryness, crusting, scaling, inflammation, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It may also be used for other purposes as determined by your doctor. This medication is available in different forms, including ointments, creams, lotions, and medicated tape. It is typically applied to the skin two or three times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as prescribed. Do not apply it to areas of the body not specified by your doctor, and avoid using more or less than directed. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area unless instructed to do so by your doctor. Before applying the medication, thoroughly wash or soak the affected area unless doing so causes irritation. Apply a thin layer of the ointment, cream, or lotion and gently rub it into the skin. If using the lotion on the scalp, part your hair, apply a small amount to the affected area, and rub it in gently. Allow the lotion to dry before washing or rubbing the area. You may wash your hair as usual, but avoid doing so immediately after applying the medication. Avoid prolonged use of flurandrenolide on the face, genital or rectal areas, skin creases, or armpits unless specifically directed by your doctor. When using flurandrenolide on a child’s diaper area, avoid tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants, as these may increase the risk of side effects. Do not apply cosmetics or other skin products to the treated area without consulting your doctor. If your doctor prescribes flurandrenolide tape, follow these steps: 1. Clean the affected area with germicidal soap and water, removing any scales or crusts, and dry the skin thoroughly. 2. 3. Cut a piece of tape slightly larger than the treatment area, rounding off the corners. Remove the white paper backing to expose the medicated surface, and avoid letting the tape stick to itself. Smooth the skin and press the tape into place. 4. Replace the tape as directed, typically every 12 hours. Remove the old tape, wash the skin, and allow the area to dry for one hour before applying a new piece. 5. If the tape loosens at the edges before it is time to replace it, trim the loose ends and apply new tape to those areas. If your doctor instructs you to wrap or bandage the treated area, follow these steps: 1. Wash or soak the area thoroughly. 2. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected area. 3. Cover the area with plastic wrap, such as Saran Wrap, ensuring the edges are sealed to adhere closely to the skin. For hands, feet, or the scalp, use plastic gloves, bags, or a shower cap, respectively. 4. If the area is moist, leave the edges of the plastic wrap unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. 5. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. 6. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time a new plastic wrap is applied. Do not stop using the medication abruptly without consulting your doctor. Before using flurandrenolide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including cancer chemotherapy agents, other topical medications, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or a history of diabetes, glaucoma, cataracts, circulation disorders, or immune system disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Flurandrenolide may cause side effects. Minor side effects include drying or cracking of the skin, acne, itching, or changes in skin color. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include severe skin rash, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, or signs of a skin infection such as redness, swelling, or oozing pus. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature and do not allow it to freeze. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and do not use it to treat other skin conditions. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share it with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Flurandrenolide is sold under the brand names Cordran®, Cordran® SP, and Cordran® Tape.
